longDescription:
Twelve reasoning-and-review skills that run in any chat, with or without tools.

- dia-intent: restates the goal, discloses assumptions and lists the decisions you must make, then waits for your approval before work starts.
- dia-elenchus: Plato's elenchus. Asks what you mean by a key idea, one question at a time, and shows where your own premises contradict each other.
- dia-brainstorm: Socratic questions one at a time, then options, a comparison by your criteria, a verdict and a brief.
- dia-reductio: strict reductio ad absurdum, with every premise listed and the contradiction derived line by line.
- dia-negative: internal critique that holds a claim to its own standard and shows where it falls short.
- dia-warrant: lays out an argument's claim, data and warrant (Toulmin) and tests the warrant with critical questions.
- dia-conjecture: tests a universal claim by counterexamples, one at a time, and repairs it with you (Lakatos).
- dia-counterplan: builds the opposing plan from your plan's key assumptions; you decide which assumptions you keep.
- dia-refine: one review pass over an answer or draft that fixes only confirmed defects.
- dia-ratchet: repeated review rounds in which only external checks count as evidence.
- dia-adjudicate: rules on reports others wrote about a text, checking each point against sources.
- dia-instruct: checks or writes text a model will follow (a skill file, a prompt, an agent file) against four rules.

The skills are instructions only: they run no code and send no data. Each skill replies in the language you write in.
capabilities: Confirm the goal, assumptions and open decisions before work starts
Run a Socratic definition dialogue (elenchus) one question at a time
Brainstorm by Socratic questions, then compare options and give a verdict
Test a claim by strict reductio ad absurdum
Critique a claim by its own standard (internal critique)
Test how well an argument's reasons support its conclusion (Toulmin, critical questions)
Test a universal claim by counterexamples; you pick the repair (Lakatos)
Build the opposing plan from a plan's key assumptions (dialectical inquiry)
Review an answer or draft once and fix confirmed defects
Run review rounds in which only outside checks count, with a round cap
Rule on reports others wrote about a text, point by point against sources
Write or review text a model follows against four rules
defaultPrompt: Use proof by contradiction on this claim: remote work always raises productivity.
Do an immanent critique of this claim: our company is flat, so anyone can speak up freely.
Socratic brainstorm with me: I need a weekend side-project idea.
